How to create a donut chart in R

You can create a donut chart in R using ggplot2. A donut chart is essentially a pie chart with a hole in the middle, which is achieved by adjusting the width of a geom_bar()-based pie chart using coord_polar().

Here’s a simple example:

Code to Create a Donut Chart in R using ggplot2

Code 
# Load required libraries
library(ggplot2)

# Create a sample dataset
data <- data.frame(
  category = c("AI", "Machine Learning", "Big Data", "Analytics"),
  value = c(30, 35, 10, 25)  # Percentages or counts
)

# Compute positions for labels
data$fraction = data$value / sum(data$value)
data$ymax = cumsum(data$fraction)
data$ymin = c(0, head(data$ymax, n=-1))

# Create the plot
ggplot(data, aes(ymax=ymax, ymin=ymin, xmax=2, xmin=1, fill=category)) +
  geom_rect() +
  coord_polar(theta="y") +  # Convert to polar coordinates
  xlim(c(0, 2)) +  # Adjust width to create a hole
  theme_void() +  # Remove unnecessary elements
  theme(legend.position = "right") +  # Adjust legend position
  labs(title="AI & Data Science Fields - Donut Chart")+
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2")+
  theme(plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#72aebc"))

Explanation

  • geom_rect(): Creates a stacked bar chart (which we later transform into a donut).

  • coord_polar(theta="y"): Converts the stacked bar into a circular format (a pie chart).

  • xlim(c(0,2)): Controls the width of the donut hole.

  • theme_void(): Removes unnecessary chart elements to focus on the data.

Code 
# Load required libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

Code 
# Create a sample dataset
data <- data.frame(
  category = c("AI", "Machine Learning", "Big Data", "Analytics"),
  value = c(30, 25, 20, 25)  # Percentages or counts
)

# Compute positions for labels
data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    fraction = value / sum(value), 
    ymax = cumsum(fraction),
    ymin = c(0, head(ymax, n=-1)),
    label = paste0(round(fraction * 100, 1), "%")  # Format labels as percentages
  )

# Define custom colours
custom_colours <- c("AI" = "#1f77b4", "Machine Learning" = "#ff7f0e", 
                    "Big Data" = "#2ca02c", "Analytics" = "#d62728")

# Create the donut chart
ggplot(data, aes(ymax=ymax, ymin=ymin, xmax=2, xmin=1, fill=category)) +
  geom_rect(colour="white") +  # Add segment borders
  geom_text(aes(x=1.5, y=(ymin+ymax)/2, label=label), size=5, colour="white") +  # Add labels
  scale_fill_manual(values=custom_colours) +  # Apply custom colours
  coord_polar(theta="y") +  # Convert to polar coordinates
  xlim(c(0, 2)) +  # Adjust width to create a hole
  theme_void() +  # Remove unnecessary elements
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.title = element_blank()) +  # Adjust legend
  labs(title="AI & Data Science Fields - Donut Chart")  # Add title

Improvements in this version:

✅ Labels: Displays percentages inside each segment for clarity
✅ Colours: Uses a custom colour palette for better visual distinction
✅ Borders: Adds white segment borders to improve readability
✅ Legend Placement: Keeps the legend on the right for a clean layout

Final Enhanced Donut Chart in R using ggplot2

Code 
# Load required libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(ggtext)  # For rich text formatting (if needed)

# Create a sample dataset
data <- data.frame(
  category = c("AI", "Machine Learning", "Big Data", "Analytics"),
  value = c(30, 25, 20, 25)  # Percentages or counts
)

# Compute positions for labels
data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    fraction = value / sum(value), 
    ymax = cumsum(fraction),
    ymin = c(0, head(ymax, n=-1)),
    label = paste0(round(fraction * 100, 1), "%")  # Format labels as percentages
  )

# Define custom colours (soft modern palette)
custom_colours <- c("AI" = "#4363d8", "Machine Learning" = "#f58231", 
                    "Big Data" = "#3cb44b", "Analytics" = "#e6194B")

# Create the donut chart
ggplot(data, aes(ymax=ymax, ymin=ymin, xmax=2, xmin=1, fill=category)) +
  geom_rect(colour="white") +  # Add segment borders
  geom_text(aes(x=1.5, y=(ymin+ymax)/2, label=label), size=5, colour="white") +  # Add labels
  scale_fill_manual(values=custom_colours) +  # Apply custom colours
  coord_polar(theta="y") +  # Convert to polar coordinates
  xlim(c(0, 2)) +  # Adjust width to create a hole
  theme_void() +  # Remove unnecessary elements
  theme(legend.position = "right", legend.title = element_blank()) +  # Adjust legend
  labs(title="AI & Data Science Fields - Donut Chart") +  # Add title
  annotate("text", x=0, y=0, label="AI & Data", size=6, fontface="bold")  # Add central text

New Features in This Version:

✅ Text in the Donut Hole: Displays "AI & Data" in the centre
✅ Improved Colour Palette: Uses a modern, soft colour scheme
✅ Better Readability: Adjusts label placement for clear visibility

library(ggplot2)

# Sample data
set.seed(123)
data <- data.frame(value = rnorm(200, mean = 50, sd = 10))

# Summary stats
mean_val <- mean(data$value)
sd_val <- sd(data$value)
median_val <- median(data$value)
q25 <- quantile(data$value, 0.25)
q75 <- quantile(data$value, 0.75)

# Plot
ggplot(data, aes(x = value)) +
  geom_density(fill = "skyblue", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = mean_val), colour = "blue", linetype = "dashed", size = 1) +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = mean_val + sd_val), colour = "red", linetype = "dotted", size = 1) +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = mean_val - sd_val), colour = "red", linetype = "dotted", size = 1) +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = median_val), colour = "darkgreen", linetype = "solid", size = 1) +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = q25), colour = "darkgreen", linetype = "dotted", size = 1) +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = q75), colour = "darkgreen", linetype = "dotted", size = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution with Summary Statistics",
    x = "Value",
    y = "Density",
    caption = paste(
      "Mean =", round(mean_val, 2),
      "SD =", round(sd_val, 2),
      "Median =", round(median_val, 2),
      "Q1 =", round(q25, 2),
      "Q3 =", round(q75, 2)
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

Code 
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# Sample data
set.seed(123)
data <- data.frame(value = rnorm(2000, mean = 50, sd = 10))

# Summary stats
mean_val <- mean(data$value)
sd_val <- sd(data$value)
median_val <- median(data$value)
q25 <- quantile(data$value, 0.25)
q75 <- quantile(data$value, 0.75)

# Compute density manually
dens <- density(data$value)
dens_df <- data.frame(x = dens$x, y = dens$y)

# Function to get y from x in density
get_y <- function(val) {
  approx(dens_df$x, dens_df$y, xout = val)$y
}

# Get y values at each stat
stat_lines <- data.frame(
  x = c(mean_val, mean_val - sd_val, mean_val + sd_val,
        median_val, q25, q75),
  colour = c("blue", "red", "red", "darkgreen", "darkgreen", "darkgreen"),
  linetype = c("dashed", "dotted", "dotted", "solid", "dotted", "dotted"),
  yend = sapply(c(mean_val, mean_val - sd_val, mean_val + sd_val,
                  median_val, q25, q75), get_y)
)

# Plot
ggplot() +
  geom_density(data = data, aes(x = value), fill = "skyblue", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_segment(data = stat_lines,
               aes(x = x, xend = x, y = 0, yend = yend, 
                   colour = colour, linetype = linetype), size = 1) +
  scale_colour_identity() +
  scale_linetype_identity() +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution with Summary Statistics (Trimmed Lines)",
    x = "Value",
    y = "Density",
    caption = paste(
      "Mean =", round(mean_val, 2),
      "SD =", round(sd_val, 2),
      "Median =", round(median_val, 2),
      "Q1 =", round(q25, 2),
      "Q3 =", round(q75, 2)
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
Code 
library(ggplot2)

# Define mean and standard deviation
mu <- 0
sigma <- 1

# Create data frame for x values
x_vals <- seq(mu - 4*sigma, mu + 4*sigma, length.out = 1000)
df <- data.frame(x = x_vals, y = dnorm(x_vals, mean = mu, sd = sigma))

# Define shaded regions
shade_data <- data.frame(
  xmin = c(mu - sigma, mu - 2*sigma, mu - 3*sigma, mu, mu + sigma, mu + 2*sigma),
  xmax = c(mu + sigma, mu - sigma, mu - 2*sigma, mu + sigma, mu + 2*sigma, mu + 3*sigma),
  fill = c("68.26%", "13.59%", "2.14%", "34.13%", "13.59%", "2.14%")
)

# Plot
ggplot(df, aes(x, y)) +
  stat_function(fun = dnorm, args = list(mean = mu, sd = sigma), colour = "darkred", size = 1.2) +
  geom_area(data = subset(df, x >= mu - sigma & x <= mu + sigma), aes(x = x, y = y), fill = "skyblue", alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_area(data = subset(df, x >= mu - 2*sigma & x < mu - sigma), aes(x = x, y = y), fill = "skyblue", alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_area(data = subset(df, x >= mu + sigma & x <= mu + 2*sigma), aes(x = x, y = y), fill = "skyblue", alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_area(data = subset(df, x >= mu - 3*sigma & x < mu - 2*sigma), aes(x = x, y = y), fill = "skyblue", alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_area(data = subset(df, x > mu + 2*sigma & x <= mu + 3*sigma), aes(x = x, y = y), fill = "skyblue", alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(mu - 3*sigma, mu - 2*sigma, mu - sigma, mu, mu + sigma, mu + 2*sigma, mu + 3*sigma),
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(mu - 3*sigma, mu - 2*sigma, mu - sigma, mu, mu + sigma, mu + 2*sigma, mu + 3*sigma),
                     labels = c("μ-3σ", "μ-2σ", "μ-σ", "μ", "μ+σ", "μ+2σ", "μ+3σ")) +
  labs(title = "Normal Distribution with Standard Deviations",
       x = "", y = "") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)
Code 
library(ggplot2)
library(grid)

mu <- 0
sigma <- 1

x_vals <- seq(mu - 4*sigma, mu + 4*sigma, length.out = 1000)
df <- data.frame(x = x_vals, y = dnorm(x_vals, mean = mu, sd = sigma))

# Base plot
p <- ggplot(df, aes(x, y)) +
  stat_function(fun = dnorm, args = list(mean = mu, sd = sigma),
                colour = "darkred", size = 1.2) +

  # Shaded regions
  geom_area(data = subset(df, x >= mu - sigma & x <= mu + sigma), aes(x = x, y = y),
            fill = "skyblue", alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_area(data = subset(df, x >= mu - 2*sigma & x < mu - sigma), aes(x = x, y = y),
            fill = "skyblue", alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_area(data = subset(df, x >= mu + sigma & x <= mu + 2*sigma), aes(x = x, y = y),
            fill = "skyblue", alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_area(data = subset(df, x >= mu - 3*sigma & x < mu - 2*sigma), aes(x = x, y = y),
            fill = "skyblue", alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_area(data = subset(df, x > mu + 2*sigma & x <= mu + 3*sigma), aes(x = x, y = y),
            fill = "skyblue", alpha = 0.2) +

  # Vertical dashed lines
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(mu - 3*sigma, mu - 2*sigma, mu - sigma, mu,
                            mu + sigma, mu + 2*sigma, mu + 3*sigma),
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +

  # X-axis labels
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(mu - 3*sigma, mu - 2*sigma, mu - sigma,
                                mu, mu + sigma, mu + 2*sigma, mu + 3*sigma),
                     labels = c("μ-3σ", "μ-2σ", "μ-σ", "μ", "μ+σ", "μ+2σ", "μ+3σ")) +

  # Arrows and percentage labels
  annotate("segment", x = mu - sigma, xend = mu + sigma, y = 0.25, yend = 0.25,
           arrow = arrow(type = "closed", length = unit(0.15, "cm"))) +
  annotate("text", x = mu, y = 0.26, label = "68.26%", size = 4) +

  annotate("segment", x = mu - 2*sigma, xend = mu + 2*sigma, y = 0.05, yend = 0.05,
           arrow = arrow(type = "closed", length = unit(0.15, "cm"))) +
  annotate("text", x = mu, y = 0.06, label = "95.44%", size = 4) +

  annotate("segment", x = mu - 3*sigma, xend = mu + 3*sigma, y = 0.0, yend = 0.0,
           arrow = arrow(type = "closed", length = unit(0.15, "cm"))) +
  annotate("text", x = mu, y = 0.01, label = "99.72%", size = 4) +

  labs(title = "Normal Distribution with Standard Deviations",
       x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)

print(p)

             linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +

  # X-axis labels

                                mu, mu + sigma, mu + 2*sigma, mu + 3*sigma),
                     labels = c("μ-3σ", "μ-2σ", "μ-σ", "μ", "μ+σ", "μ+2σ", "μ+3σ")) +

  # Arrows and percentage labels
  annotate("segment", x = mu - sigma, xend = mu + sigma, y = 0.25, yend = 0.25,
           arrow = arrow(type = "closed", length = unit(0.15, "cm"))) +
  annotate("text", x = mu, y = 0.26, label = "68.26%", size = 4) +

  annotate("segment", x = mu - 2*sigma, xend = mu + 2*sigma, y = 0.05, yend = 0.05,

  annotate("text", x = mu, y = 0.06, label = "95.44%", size = 4) +

  annotate("segment", x = mu - 3*sigma, xend = mu + 3*sigma, y = 0.0, yend = 0.0,
           arrow = arrow(type = "closed", length = unit(0.15, "cm"))) +
  annotate("text", x = mu, y = 0.01, label = "99.72%", size = 4) +

  # Text labels inside shaded areas
  annotate("text", x = mu + 0.5, y = - 0.01, label = "34.13%", size = 4) +
  annotate("text", x = mu - 0.5, y = - 0.01, label = "34.13%", size = 4) +
  annotate("text", x = mu - 1.5*sigma, y = - 0.01, label = "13.59%", size = 4) +
  annotate("text", x = mu + 1.5*sigma, y = - 0.01, label = "13.59%", size = 4) +

  annotate("text", x = mu + 2.5*sigma, y = - 0.01, label = "2.14%", size = 4) +

  labs(title = "Normal Distribution with Shaded Areas and Percentages",
       x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)

print(p)
